\begin{abstract}
\begin{outline}{Abstract, 0.3 page}
\item Problem: a long/short pod under a platform's neutrality mandate at a fixed \RiskBudgetPct\%/yr risk budget $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:setting}.
\item Approach: duals of the convex program at a root-found $\lambda^*$; three integer sensitivity estimators against certified secant intervals; big-M against perspective formulations $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:approach}.
\item Q1 finding: liquidity and sector bounds carry the cost; factor neutrality is nearly free for $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ $\rightarrow$ \ELiqMed, \ESectorMed, \IdealRetMomMin; Figs.~\ref{fig:costcurves}--\ref{fig:alignment}.
\item Q2 finding: with integers, no continuous estimator recovers the secant; the fixed-integer dual is exact only when the support does not change $\rightarrow$ Table~\ref{tab:i1}, \PredOneMax, \PredThreeMed.
\item Q3 finding: the perspective relaxation is tighter, but default scaling defeats it; rescaling the weights fixes it $\rightarrow$ \KTwentyFourMed, \RootDefBase, \RootRescBase; Fig.~\ref{fig:formulations}.
\end{outline}
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}
\begin{outline}{I, 0.8 page}
\item Motivation and significance: a multi-manager platform imposes neutrality to protect its other books; each constraint costs the pod expected alpha; the dual is the price of that constraint $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:setting}.
\item Related work: fundamental law and transfer coefficient \cite{grinold2000active,clarke2002portfolio}; constraint attribution \cite{stubbs2010constraint}; factor alignment \cite{lee2008risk,ceria2012factor}; realistic shorts \cite{jacobs2005portfolio}; perspective reformulations \cite{frangioni2006perspective,gunluk2010perspective}; integer sensitivity \cite{geoffrion1977parametric,wolsey1981integer}; sparse portfolios \cite{bertsimas2022scalable}; course texts \cite{boyd2004convex,wolsey2020integer}.
\item Questions Q1--Q3 (DESIGN §2) $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:results}.
\item Contribution: costs at equal risk via duality at $\lambda^*$, with the alignment closed form $\sqrt{1-\varphi}$ $\rightarrow$ A1--A4, Fig.~\ref{fig:alignment}.
\item Contribution: certified secant intervals that test integer sensitivity estimators against solver error $\rightarrow$ A8, Table~\ref{tab:i1}, \WidthMed.
\item Contribution: a support-stability account of when the fixed-integer dual is exact $\rightarrow$ \PredOneMax\ (P1), \PredThreeMed\ (P3).
\item Contribution: weight rescaling as the fix for the perspective cones' absolute tolerance $\rightarrow$ A9, Sec.~\ref{sec:results-q3}, \ConeRescMax, Table~\ref{tab:n2}.
\item Project type: problem formulation, reusing published formulations in a new setting.
\end{outline}

\section{Problem Setting}
\label{sec:setting}

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Decision problem}
A long/short equity pod at a multi-manager platform receives each month a forecast $\alpha_i$ of every stock's \emph{alpha}, its expected return beyond what its factor exposures explain, and chooses weights $w$ as fractions of assets under management (AUM, \$\AUMBillion B). The platform caps the pod's ex-ante volatility at \RiskBudgetPct\%/yr and imposes a mandate that protects its other books. A portfolio's \emph{factor exposure} is $y=B\T w$, where $B$ holds each stock's loadings on six factors; its \emph{beta} is the exposure $y_{\mathrm{mkt}}$ to the market factor. \emph{Dollar neutrality} bounds the net weight $|1\T w|$, \emph{beta neutrality} bounds $|y_{\mathrm{mkt}}|$, style neutrality bounds the other five exposures, and \emph{sector neutrality} bounds each sector's net weight $|S_j\T w|$. \emph{Gross leverage} $1\T(w^++w^-)$ is the total long plus short weight. A stock's \emph{average daily volume} (ADV) is measured as its median daily dollar volume over the last \AdvWindow\ trading days, and the \emph{liquidity cap} limits each position to the fraction $\theta$ of ADV: $u_i=\min(u,\theta\,\mathrm{ADV}_i/\mathrm{AUM})$. Shorts pay a \emph{borrow cost} $c$ per month and every trade a one-way \emph{trading cost} $\kappa$; the pod starts from cash ($w_0=0$), so the trading cost is $\kappa$ times gross. Table~\ref{tab:mandate} lists the base mandate.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Data and risk model}
Daily adjusted prices and volumes of the current S\&P~500 constituents (\PanelTickers\ tickers, \PanelStart\ to \PanelEnd, \PanelDays\ trading days) come from yfinance, GICS sectors from the constituent list, and the daily Fama--French five factors and momentum from the French data library \cite{fama2015five,french_data_library,yfinance}. At each of the \RiskMonthEnds\ month-ends from \RiskFirst\ to \RiskLast, the risk model regresses each eligible stock's trailing \RiskWindow\ daily returns on the six factors. $B$ holds the loadings, $D=\mathrm{diag}(d)$ the monthly residual variances, floored at the \FloorPct th cross-sectional percentile, and $F$ the monthly factor covariance, so $\Sigma=BFB\T+D\succ 0$. The eligible universe has \UnivMin--\UnivMax\ names. The continuous experiments use the dates D12 = \{\DTwelve\}, chosen to span calm and stressed markets.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Alphas and alignment}
The momentum alpha $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ is each stock's return over the year before the date, skipping the last month, z-scored across the universe, winsorized at $\pm\WinsorClip$, re-standardized, and scaled as $\alpha_i=\ICAssumed\sqrt{d_i}\,z_i$. It is an input signal, not a strategy; no backtest is run. A $D^{-1}$-weighted least-squares regression of $\alpha$ on the loadings splits it into a residual $\alpha_\perp=\alpha-B(B\T D^{-1}B)^{-1}B\T D^{-1}\alpha$ and a factor-spanned part $\alpha_\parallel=\alpha-\alpha_\perp$. The \emph{information ratio} $\sqrt{\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha}$ is the best attainable ratio of expected alpha to ex-ante risk. The \emph{alignment share} $\varphi=\alpha_\parallel\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\parallel/\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha\in[0,1]$ is the fraction of its square carried by the factors. For comparisons, $\alpha_\perp$ and $\alpha_\parallel$ are rescaled to $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$'s information ratio. The \emph{transfer coefficient} of a portfolio is the correlation, in the $\Sigma$ metric, between $w$ and the unconstrained direction $\Sigma^{-1}\alpha$: $\mathrm{TC}=\alpha\T w/(\sqrt{\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha}\sqrt{w\T\Sigma w})$ \cite{clarke2002portfolio}.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{The convex problem \prb}
With $w=w^+-w^-$, $w^\pm\ge0$, and $\sigma_m$ the monthly volatility budget,
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\max\ & \alpha\T w-c\,1\T w^- -\kappa\,1\T(w^++w^-)\\
\text{s.t.}\ & y\T Fy+\textstyle\sum_i d_iw_i^2\le\sigma_m^2,\quad y=B\T w,\\
& |1\T w|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{net}},\ |y_{\mathrm{mkt}}|\le\varepsilon_\beta,\ |y_k|\le b_k,\ |S_j\T w|\le s_j,\\
& 1\T(w^++w^-)\le G,\quad w_i^+,w_i^-\le u_i .
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:prb}
\end{equation}
Absolute values and costs are linear through the split $w^\pm$; because $c,\kappa>0$, at most one of $w_i^\pm$ is positive at an optimum. The optimal value $A^*$ is net expected alpha per month. Each bound $b_j$ has a dual $\mu_j$ (the sum of its two one-sided multipliers) and an \emph{elasticity} $e_j=\mu_jb_j/A^*$, the percent change in alpha per percent change in the bound; a constraint \emph{binds} if $e_j\ge\BindTol$. The risk row's multiplier is written $\lambda^*$. It is the Lagrange multiplier of the risk budget: the price of risk at which a mean-variance investor chooses the same portfolio (A1). Fixing the risk budget rather than $\lambda$ compares constraint costs at equal risk, so relaxing a constraint cannot buy alpha by levering up.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{The integer problem \pmi}
\pmi\ adds a cardinality limit $K$ and a minimum position $\ell=\MinPositionPct\%$, moves the risk row into the objective at its multiplier, and raises the position cap to $u=\MiqpPositionPct\%$:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\max\ & \alpha\T w-\lambda^*\big(y\T Fy+\textstyle\sum_i d_iw_i^2\big)\\
& \quad -c\,1\T w^- -\kappa\,1\T(w^++w^-)\\
\text{s.t.}\ & \text{the mandate of \eqref{eq:prb} without the risk row},\\
& \ell z_i^\pm\le w_i^\pm\le u_iz_i^\pm,\ z_i^++z_i^-\le1,\ \textstyle\sum_i(z_i^++z_i^-)\le K,\\
& z^\pm\in\{0,1\}^N .
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:pmi}
\end{equation}
$\lambda^*$ is \prb's multiplier on the same universe at the base mandate with $u=\MiqpPositionPct\%$, held fixed for that date and universe. \pmi\ is then the same pod with integer constraints added: a Lagrangian relaxation of the risk row, with zero gap in the convex case. The \emph{big-M} formulation keeps $\sum_id_iw_i^2$ with $M=u_i$. The \emph{perspective} formulation replaces it by $\sum_id_is_i$ with rotated cones $w_i^2\le s_i\zeta_i$, $s_i\ge0$, where $\zeta_i=z_i^++z_i^-$. The \emph{rescaled perspective} is the same model with every weight divided by the largest position bound $\max_iu_i$, and each cone written in its own name's bound, $t_i=w_i/u_i$ and $s_i'=s_i/u_i^2$, so that $t_i^2\le s_i'\zeta_i$ with $t_i,s_i'$ of order one. Its feasible set and objective are unchanged; only the quantities Gurobi's absolute tolerances act on differ (A9).

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Problem classes}
\prb\ is a convex quadratically constrained program (QCQP); its risk row is the second-order cone $\|(L_F\T y,\sqrt d\circ w)\|_2\le\sigma_m$ with $F=L_FL_F\T$. When the risk row binds the optimum is unique, because a linear objective over a strictly convex set attains its maximum at a single point. The big-M \pmi\ is a convex mixed-integer QP, every node relaxation a convex QP; the perspective \pmi\ is a mixed-integer second-order cone program.

\section{Solution Approach and Analysis}
\label{sec:approach}

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Algorithms}
\prb\ is solved as the mean-variance QP $\max\ \alpha\T w-\lambda w\T\Sigma w-\text{costs}$ by Gurobi's dual simplex at feasibility and optimality tolerances \QPTol, with $\lambda$ found by Brent's method on $\log\lambda$ so that ex-ante volatility equals the budget to relative \RootRtol. A1 makes this exact, and dual simplex returns exact active sets and duals; if $\lambda=\LambdaMin$ still leaves volatility below the budget, the risk row is slack. Clarabel's primal--dual interior-point method \cite{goulart2024clarabel} (tolerances \ClarabelTol) solves the explicit cone form of \eqref{eq:prb} as a cross-check. It also computes the perspective relaxation of \eqref{eq:pmi} ($z\in[0,1]$), whose central finite differences give its slope; Clarabel's raw duals are kept as diagnostics. The big-M relaxation and the fixed-integer QP (\pmi\ with $z$ fixed at the incumbent) are QPs solved by dual simplex. Gurobi's branch and bound solves \pmi\ \cite{gurobi2026manual}, with its MIQCP method left at the default for the perspective model. The \pmi\ objective is multiplied by $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObj$ so that its value is of order one relative to the solver's tolerances, and every value is reported in original units. Effort is Gurobi's deterministic Work, with WorkLimit $W^*=\WStar$ (\IOneWorkFactor$W^*$ in I1 and I2). The incumbent is \emph{polished}: the fixed-integer QP at its $z$ is re-solved at tolerances \PolishTol, and that value is $V$.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\subsection{Analysis}
\textbf{A1 (risk budget and mean-variance).} With multiplier $\mu$ for the risk row and $\nu$ for the mandate rows, the Lagrangian of \eqref{eq:prb} is $\alpha\T w-\text{costs}-\mu(w\T\Sigma w-\sigma_m^2)-\nu\T(\text{mandate})$. Its stationarity condition is that of the mean-variance problem with $\lambda=\mu$, and under Slater's condition (A5) the KKT conditions are necessary and sufficient. So the mean-variance optimum at $\lambda=\mu_{\mathrm{risk}}$ solves \prb: the risk budget is an $\varepsilon$-constraint and $\lambda^*$ its scalarization weight.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A2--A3 (equality case).} With only $Aw=0$ and a binding risk row, stationarity gives $w^*=\Sigma^{-1}g/(2\mu)$ with $g=\alpha-A\T\nu$; $Aw^*=0$ gives $\nu=(A\Sigma^{-1}A\T)^{-1}A\Sigma^{-1}\alpha$; the binding row gives $\mu=\sqrt{g\T\Sigma^{-1}g}/(2\sigma_m)$ and $A^*=\sigma_m\sqrt{g\T\Sigma^{-1}g}$. Divided by the unconstrained value $\sigma_m\sqrt{\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha}$, the retained fraction $\sqrt{g\T\Sigma^{-1}g/\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha}$ equals TC at $w^*$. It is at most one by Cauchy--Schwarz in the $\Sigma^{-1}$ metric, since $g$ is the $\Sigma^{-1}$-orthogonal projection of $\alpha$ onto $\{v:A\Sigma^{-1}v=0\}$.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A4 (alignment).} By Woodbury, $B\T\Sigma^{-1}=F^{-1}(F^{-1}+B\T D^{-1}B)^{-1}B\T D^{-1}$. The regression residual satisfies $B\T D^{-1}\alpha_\perp=0$, hence $B\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\perp=0$ and $\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\perp=D^{-1}\alpha_\perp$. Under the risk budget alone, $\alpha_\perp$'s optimum therefore has zero factor exposure, and factor bounds have zero shadow price. Because $\alpha_\parallel=B\gamma$ for the regression coefficients $\gamma$, the cross term $\alpha_\perp\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\parallel$ vanishes and $\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha=\alpha_\perp\T D^{-1}\alpha_\perp+\alpha_\parallel\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\parallel$. A2 with $A=B\T$ gives $g=\alpha_\perp$, so full factor neutrality retains $\sqrt{1-\varphi}$ of the alpha.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A5 (envelope).} $w=0$ strictly satisfies the risk row and the other constraints are affine, so Slater's condition holds, and strong duality with it. $A^*(b)$ is the perturbation function of a convex program, hence concave, and nondecreasing because loosening $b$ enlarges the feasible set \cite{boyd2004convex}. $dA^*/db_j=\mu_j$ wherever $\mu_j$ is unique (for example under LICQ), including across nondegenerate active-set changes, where $\mu_j(b)$ has a kink but $A^*$ does not.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A6 (perspective tightness).} For $z\in(0,1]$, $s\ge w^2/z\ge w^2$, so in the relaxation the perspective's risk penalty is at least big-M's and its value at most big-M's: its bound is at least as tight. The perspective of a convex function is convex, and the perspective reformulation is the closure of the perspective cuts \cite{frangioni2006perspective,gunluk2010perspective}.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A7 (one-asset toy).} For $\max\,aw-\lambda dw^2$ over $w\in\{0\}\cup[\ell,u]$, $w\le b$, the value jumps by $a\ell-\lambda d\ell^2$ at $b=\ell$. Below $\ell$, the big-M relaxation's slope is $a-2\lambda db$, the perspective relaxation's (minimizing $s$ over $z\in[w/u,w/\ell]$) is $a-\lambda d\ell$, and the fixed-integer dual is 0, which is locally correct. A tighter bound need not give a better slope.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A8 (integer value functions).} The \pmi\ value $U^*(b)$ is the upper envelope, over support patterns, of concave pieces: nondecreasing by feasible-set inclusion, but in general neither concave nor continuous. The relaxation dual is the slope of an upper-bounding concave function, the fixed-integer dual the slope of the active piece, and a re-solve gives a secant across pieces. For a bound perturbed by $\pm\delta$, $V\le U^*\le B_{\mathrm{eff}}$ holds at each point, with $V$ the polished value, $B$ the final bound and $B_{\mathrm{eff}}=\max(B,V)+\BeffSlack|V|$ (the slack covers Gurobi's tolerances). This gives the certified interval
\begin{equation}
L=\frac{V_+-B_{\mathrm{eff},-}}{2\delta}\le\frac{U^*_+-U^*_-}{2\delta}\le\frac{B_{\mathrm{eff},+}-V_-}{2\delta}=H,
\end{equation}
with point slope $s=(V_+-V_-)/(2\delta)$. A case is \emph{binding} iff $L>0$; $H<0$ is impossible at true optima and flags solver error. In I1 and I2 both formulations are solved at every point, $V$ is the larger polished value and $B$ the smaller bound (combined certification).

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A9 (scaling).} An absolute tolerance $\tau$ on a quantity of size $m$ is a relative error $\tau/m$, so rescaling a row or the objective gives an equivalent problem with different effective tolerances. The variance row has size $\sigma_m^2=\SigmaMSq$. The perspective cones $w_i^2\le s_i\zeta_i$ have $s_i$ at most $u_i^2$ and, for a held name, at least $\ell^2$, so Gurobi's absolute feasibility tolerance \GurobiFeasTol\ is a relative error of up to $\GurobiFeasTol/\ell^2$ on the smallest cones. Writing each cone in its name's bound makes that tolerance relative. The objective effect of cone violation, $\lambda^*\sum_id_i\max(0,w_i^2/\zeta_i-s_i)$ at the raw incumbent, is reported relative to $|V|$.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Finite differences and noise}
The perspective relaxation's slope is the central difference $\hat s=(R(b+\delta_r)-R(b-\delta_r))/(2\delta_r)$ of its Clarabel values $R$ at $\delta_r=\PerspFdStep\,b$. The value is the objective at Clarabel's $(w,\zeta)$ with each $s_i$ set to $w_i^2/\zeta_i$, so every cone holds exactly. A relaxation fails if its residuals exceed \RelaxResidual\ or its duality gap exceeds \RelaxGap$\max(|R|,|R_{\mathrm{ref}}|)$, where $R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the value at the unperturbed bound. That accuracy bounds the difference's noise by $\eta=\RelaxGap\max(|R|,|R_{\mathrm{ref}}|)/\delta_r$. The three-point one-sided slopes are recorded too; if they differ by more than $\max(\SlopeKinkTol|\hat s|,\SlopeKinkNoise\eta)$, with $\hat s$ the central slope, the case is flagged as a kink.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Validation}
The test suite (\TestsPassed\ passing tests) and logged check runs confirm the analysis numerically, each check with a negative control. The root-found QP and the Clarabel QCQP agree on $A^*$ to \KFourA, on $\lambda^*$ to \KFourLam\ and on $w$ to \KFourW\ (A1). The equality cases match A2--A3 to \KSixA, and the A4 split holds to \KFiveSplit. On \KNineToys\ one-asset toys (\KNinePoints\ grid points) both \pmi\ formulations match A7's value function to \KNineErr. The \KNineBand\ points just below $\ell$, within Gurobi's feasibility tolerance, where the solver may hold a name at $b<\ell$, are excluded and counted. Certified intervals contain the exact slope on \KTenToy\ toy and \KTenMip\ small MIQP cases solved to zero gap, and the $H<0$ flag fires on a constructed case. An independent feasibility checker, sharing no code with the optimizer, fails on constructed violations and passes every C1--C3 solution and every polished \pmi\ value; the N2(b) solver comparisons are measured against a reference solution instead. \pmi\ with $K\ge N$ and $\ell=0$ equals \prb\ to \KThirteen. The slope method was gated before I1 on \KTwentyNineCToys\ random toys, with \KTwentyNineCMisses\ misses at \KTwentyNineCPoints\ points, \KTwentyNineCPairMisses\ of \KTwentyNineCPairs\ objective-scale pairs outside tolerance, and a failed fraction of \KTwentyNineCFailedFrac.

\section{Results}
\label{sec:results}

\subsection{Q1: Constraint Costs in the Convex Problem}
\label{sec:results-q1}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Setup.} C1 solves \prb\ at the base mandate ($u=\BasePositionPct\%$) on the full universe at the \NDTwelve\ D12 dates for each of the three alphas (\CNPoints\ solves). C2 sweeps one constraint family at a time with all others at base (\CTwoN\ solves). The criterion is the elasticity $e_j$, read from exact duals, which are validated as derivatives below. Statistics are over the D12 dates for $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ ($n=\NDTwelve$) unless stated.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Which constraints bind.} At base, $A^*$ has median \AMomMedBp\ bp/month (range \AMomMinBp--\AMomMaxBp), and the pod keeps a median \RetMomMed\ (\RetMomMin--\RetMomMax) of the alpha of the unconstrained, costless optimum. The risk budget binds in all but \CSlack\ of the \CNPoints\ C1 solves, all of them $\alpha_\parallel$. The liquidity cap binds at all \ELiqBind\ dates with median elasticity \ELiqMed, sector bounds at \ESectorBind\ (median \ESectorMed) and dollar neutrality at \EDollarBind\ (median \EDollarMed). Style bounds bind at \EStyleBind\ dates and the position cap at \EPosBind; beta and gross bind at none. Fig.~\ref{fig:costcurves} shows the cost curves. At the tightest grid points the pod keeps a median \CTwoLiqTight\ of its alpha at $\theta=\LiqTightPct\%$ (range \CTwoLiqTightMin--\CTwoLiqTightMax), \CTwoSectorTight\ under exact sector neutrality (\CTwoSectorTightMin--\CTwoSectorTightMax), \CTwoStyleTight\ with every style exposure at zero, \CTwoDollarTight\ under exact dollar neutrality and \CTwoBetaTight\ under exact beta neutrality.

\begin{figure}[!t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{../figures/fig1_cost_curves.pdf}
\caption{Cost curves (C2): retained alpha $A^*(b)/A^*(\mathrm{off})$ against each family's bound, all other constraints at base. Solid: the $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ median with its interquartile band over the \NDTwelve\ D12 dates; for factor families, the $\alpha_\perp$ (dashed) and $\alpha_\parallel$ (dash-dotted) medians.}
\label{fig:costcurves}
\end{figure}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{What determines the cost.} Factor bounds are cheap because $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ is weakly aligned with the factors: its alignment share $\varphi$ is \PhiMomMin--\PhiMomMax\ over D12. Under idealized full factor neutrality (risk budget only) the retained fraction equals $\sqrt{1-\varphi}$ (A4), at least \IdealRetMomMin\ for $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ (Fig.~\ref{fig:alignment}). The numerical and closed-form fractions agree to \IdealRetErr\ over \IdealFactorN\ solves, and $A^*$ to \IdealARelErr\ relative where the closed form is nonzero (\IdealNonzeroN\ solves) and to \IdealZeroAbs\ absolute where it is zero (the \IdealZeroN\ $\alpha_\parallel$ solves). The two extremes bracket this: $\alpha_\perp$ has $\varphi\le\PhiPerpMax$ and loses nothing, while $\alpha_\parallel$ has $\varphi=\PhiParMax$ and loses everything. At the base mandate the points lie well below the curve, so the cost comes from the caps and the costs, not from neutrality. The attribution of Fig.~\ref{fig:attribution} agrees: the position and liquidity caps carry a median share \AttPosMed\ of the attributed loss, trading costs \AttTradeMed, sector bounds \AttSectorMed, borrow \AttBorrowMed, and names held at zero \AttInactiveMed.

Filled: idealized full factor neutrality with the risk budget only (three alphas $\times$ \NDTwelve\ dates). Hollow: the base mandate. Both are relative to the unconstrained, costless \prb.}

The stacked total exceeds the fixed-risk loss $A^*_{\mathrm{unc}}-A^*$ (markers) because the unconstrained portfolio at $\lambda^*$ carries more than the \RiskBudgetPct\%/yr budget.}
\label{fig:attribution}
\end{figure}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Duals as derivatives.} For every binding constraint at every D12 date (\KFifteenN\ checks), the dual $\mu_j$ is compared with the central difference at $\delta=\EnvStepPct\%$ of the bound. The \KFifteenFlag\ stencils whose dual vanishes at an end, or whose forward and backward differences differ by more than \KinkPct\% of the central one, are rechecked at $\delta=\EnvFineStepPct\%$. After the recheck the largest error is \KFifteenMaxErr\ and \KFifteenOver\ exceed \KinkPct\%; at $\delta=\EnvStepPct\%$ alone the worst error is \KFifteenCoarseWorst, at a flagged stencil. Of the flagged points, \KinkAS\ have an active-set change within the stencil (a mandate row, a cap, or a name entering or leaving the support) and \KinkCurv\ are curvature flags; \UnflaggedAS\ of the \Unflagged\ unflagged points also change their active set within the stencil. Shrinking the step tenfold shrinks the gap between the forward and backward differences by a factor of \RatioMin--\RatioMax\ at all \RatioNearTenth\ flagged points, as on a smooth piece: at this resolution $A^*(b)$ is differentiable even across active-set changes, as A5 predicts. Along all \KSeventeenSweeps\ C2 sweeps, $A^*$ never decreases as a bound loosens (\KSeventeenPairs\ pairs) and the secant slopes never increase (\KSeventeenTriples\ triples) beyond tolerance: \KSeventeenFail\ failures.

\subsection{Q2: Sensitivity under Integrality}
\label{sec:results-q2}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Setup.} I1 solves \pmi\ at \DIa, \DIb\ and \DIc\ on the top \IOneN\ names by ADV, with $K=\mathrm{round}(fS)$ for $f\in\{\Fa,\Fb,\Fc\}$ and $S$ the continuous support size. Four constraints are perturbed by $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$ of their bound: sector and dollar at \BaseSectorPct\%, all styles jointly at \BaseStyle, and the momentum exposure bound, tightened from its base value to \MomBound; at \IOneRobustDate\ also by $\delta=\IOneRobustDeltaPct\%$. That gives \IOneCases\ cases, \IOneCasesTen\ at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$ and \IOneCasesFive\ at $\delta=\IOneRobustDeltaPct\%$. Each point is solved with big-M and the rescaled perspective at MIPGap \IOneMipGap\ under combined certification. The estimators are the big-M relaxation dual, the perspective relaxation slope and the fixed-integer dual. The \emph{continuous baseline} is \pmi\ with $\ell=0$ and no cardinality row, the convex reference. The criterion is each estimator's relative error $|\hat\mu-s|/|s|$ over binding cases, and whether $\hat\mu\in[L,H]$.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Certification.} No certified interval is violated (\KTwentyThreeViol\ of \KTwentyThreePoints\ points), and the polished values of the two formulations were identical at all \VTieIOne\ I1 points; the bound came from big-M at \BFromBigM\ points and from the rescaled perspective at \BFromResc. At $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$, \IOneBindTen\ of \IOneCasesTen\ cases bind (sector \IOneBindSector, momentum \IOneBindMom, dollar \IOneBindDollar, all styles \IOneBindStyle). In the \IOneNonBindTen\ non-binding cases at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$, and the \IOneNonBindFive\ at $\delta=\IOneRobustDeltaPct\%$, all three estimators are zero (the perspective slope to within \NonBindPerspMax). The intervals are narrow but not points: at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$ the relative width $(H-L)/s$ over the \WidthN\ binding cases has median \WidthMed\ (range \WidthMin--\WidthMax), set by $B_{\mathrm{eff}}$'s slack. Lying in $[L,H]$ therefore means agreeing with the secant to within that width.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Estimator errors.} Table~\ref{tab:i1} gives the errors at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$ ($n=\IOneBindTen$). The perspective slope has the smallest median error, \ErrPerspMed\ (interquartile range \ErrPerspLo--\ErrPerspHi, max \ErrPerspMax). The fixed-integer dual follows with \ErrFixedMed\ (\ErrFixedLo--\ErrFixedHi, max \ErrFixedMax), and the big-M dual is worst, \ErrBigMMed\ (\ErrBigMLo--\ErrBigMHi, max \ErrBigMMax). Only \ErrFixedInLH\ estimates, all fixed-integer duals, lie in $[L,H]$. The convex baseline's dual is within a median \BaseSecMed\ (max \BaseSecMax, $n=\BaseSecN$) of its own secant at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$, so integrality, not the step, accounts for the error. Only the big-M error falls at each step of $f$, and so of $K/S$; the perspective error is flat from $f=\Fb$, and the fixed-integer error is not monotone. The errors depend on $\delta$. At \IOneRobustDate\ ($n=\RobustN$ binding of \RobustCases\ at each step), the median errors at $\delta=\IOneRobustDeltaPct\%$ and \IOneDeltaPct\% are \RobustBigMFive\ and \RobustBigMTen\ for big-M, \RobustPerspFive\ and \RobustPerspTen\ for the perspective, and \RobustFixedFive\ and \RobustFixedTen\ for the fixed-integer dual.

Bottom: the convex baseline's dual against its own secant at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$.}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{When the fixed-integer dual is exact.} Each case is classed by comparing, at $b-\delta$, $b$ and $b+\delta$, the support of $V$'s incumbent (sign included) and the fixed-integer QP's active set. P1 means both unchanged, P2 the support unchanged but the active set changed, P3 the support changed. Of the \SupBind\ binding cases, \SupPOneTen, \SupPTwoTen\ and \SupPThreeTen\ are P1, P2 and P3 at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$, and \SupPOneFive, \SupPTwoFive\ and \SupPThreeFive\ at $\delta=\IOneRobustDeltaPct\%$. Pooling both steps, in P1 the fixed-integer error is at most \PredOneMax\ ($n=\PredOneN$; predicted $\le\PredOneTol$), and in P2 at most \PredTwoMax\ ($n=\PredTwoN$; predicted $\le$\PredTwoTol, the baseline's largest secant error). In P3 its median is \PredThreeMed\ and its max \PredThreeMax\ ($n=\PredThreeN$). Every fixed-integer estimate in $[L,H]$ (\FixedLHTen\ at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$, \FixedLHFive\ at \IOneRobustDeltaPct\%) is in P1 or P2. The relaxation slopes fail differently. At $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$ the median perspective error is \ClassPerspPOne\ in P1 ($n=\SupPOneTen$) and \ClassPerspPThree\ in P3 ($n=\SupPThreeTen$), and it rises with the relaxation's gap at $b$: the Spearman rank correlation (average ranks) between gap and error is \SpearmanPersp\ for the perspective and \SpearmanBigM\ for big-M ($n=\SpearmanN$).

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Value functions.} I2 sweeps the sector bound, the I1 constraint with the largest median secant at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$ (\NearTieSector, against \NearTieMom\ for the momentum bound), over \ITwoPoints\ points on $[0,\ITwoGridMult b]$ at \DIb\ ($K=\ITwoKa$) and \DIc\ ($K=\ITwoKb$), with \IOneN\ names (Fig.~\ref{fig:valuefunctions}). The \pmi\ value lies below the continuous baseline, and its grid secants are not monotone. At \DIb, \GridCertA\ of \GridTriplesA\ grid triples are certified nonconcave, $V(b_{k-1})+V(b_{k+1})>2B_{\mathrm{eff}}(b_k)$; at \DIc, \GridCertB\ of \GridTriplesB. Every nonconcavity seen in $V$ alone is certified (\GridUncertA\ and \GridUncertB). The support changes between \GridSupChA\ of \GridPairsA\ and \GridSupChB\ of \GridPairsB\ neighbouring points, by \GridNamesMin--\GridNamesMax\ names. At $\ITwoFracLo b$, $b$ and $\ITwoFracHi b$, each with $\delta=\ITwoDeltaPct\%$ of that bound ($n=\ITwoN$), the median errors are \ITwoBigMMed\ (big-M), \ITwoPerspMed\ (perspective) and \ITwoFixedMed\ (fixed-integer), and none lies in its interval, whose relative width is at most \ITwoWidthMax. The baseline's dual matches its envelope slope within \KinkPct\% at all \ITwoEnvN\ grid points with $b>0$ (of \ITwoNPoints).

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Slope accuracy.} None of the \PerspRelax\ I1 perspective relaxations failed and \PerspKinks\ kinks were flagged; over the \RawDualN\ binding I1 cases at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$, Clarabel's raw duals agree with the finite-difference slope to a median relative \RawDualMed\ (max \RawDualMax). The slopes do not depend on the objective scale: at \KTwentyNineBScale\ times $s_{\mathrm{obj}}$ they agree within tolerance in all \KTwentyNineBN\ gated cases at \DIa\ and in all \ExtN\ remaining cases (over the \ExtBindN\ of those cases that bind, at either step, the largest relative difference is \ExtBindDiff).

\subsection{Q3: Formulations and Numerics}
\label{sec:results-q3}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Setup.} N1 solves \pmi\ at \DNa\ and \DNb\ with $N\in\{\NOneSmallN,\NOneMidN,\text{all eligible}\}$ and $f\in\{\Fa,\Fb\}$, at three tightness levels: loose (styles \LooseStyle, beta \LooseBeta), base, and tight (\TightStyle, \TightBeta). Each instance is solved by big-M, the perspective at default scaling and the rescaled perspective, at MIPGap \NOneMipGap\ and WorkLimit $W^*$ (\NOneSolves\ solves, including a presolve-off repeat at $N=\NOneMidN$). The plain relaxations are the $z\in[0,1]$ relaxations solved directly, without presolve or cuts. The criteria are Work and the root gap, (root bound $-$ best known value)$/|$best known value$|$, taken after Gurobi's root cut loop. Each cell of Fig.~\ref{fig:formulations} has $n=\NOneCell$ instances. Default-scaling results are reported as solver behaviour: they describe how Gurobi treats the unscaled cones, not the formulation.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Root gaps and effort.} At default presolve the rescaled perspective has the smallest median root gap at loose and base tightness and big-M at tight (rescaled \RootRescLoose, \RootRescBase, \RootRescTight; big-M \RootBigMLoose, \RootBigMBase, \RootBigMTight, for loose, base, tight). The rescaled perspective does the least Work at every level (\WorkRescLoose, \WorkRescBase, \WorkRescTight; big-M \WorkBigMLoose, \WorkBigMBase, \WorkBigMTight). The default-scaling perspective is far behind (\RootDefLoose, \RootDefBase, \RootDefTight) and does the most Work (\WorkDefLoose, \WorkDefBase, \WorkDefTight). No solve at default presolve stopped at the WorkLimit. The plain relaxations order as A6 predicts: on every instance the perspective relaxation's value is at most big-M's (\KTwentyFourViol\ violations), by a median margin of \KTwentyFourMed\ of $|V|$ (range \KTwentyFourMin--\KTwentyFourMax). At base, the median plain gaps are \PlainBigMBase\ for big-M and \PlainPerspBase\ for the perspective. Big-M's root gap is two orders of magnitude below its plain relaxation's, and Gurobi's presolve does that work. At $N=\NOneMidN$ ($n=\PreN$ per arm), turning presolve off raises big-M's median root gap from \PreBigMRootOn\ to \PreBigMRootOff\ (its plain gap is \PrePlainBigM) and its median Work from \PreBigMWorkOn\ to \PreBigMWorkOff, with \PreBigMCensOff\ solves stopped at the WorkLimit. The rescaled perspective moves only from \PreRescRootOn\ to \PreRescRootOff\ (Work \PreRescWorkOn\ to \PreRescWorkOff), near its plain gap of \PrePlainPersp.

\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{../figures/fig5_formulations.pdf}
\caption{N1: root gap after the root cut loop (top) and Work (bottom) against mandate tightness, default presolve; one marker per instance ($n=\NOneCell$ per cell), medians connected. The default-scaling perspective is solver behaviour. Thin gray lines mark the median plain-relaxation gaps of big-M (dotted) and the perspective (dashed).}
\label{fig:formulations}
\end{figure}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Agreement and cone tolerance.} Every arm's polished value lies within every other arm's $B_{\mathrm{eff}}$ (\KTwentyTwoFail\ failures in \KTwentyTwoPairs\ pairs). The worst $|\Delta V|$ uses \KTwentyTwoWorstDef\ (big-M against default scaling) and \KTwentyTwoWorstResc\ (against the rescaled arm) of the larger certified gap. Reruns under the WorkLimit are identical (\KTwentyFiveSame\ of \KTwentyFiveN). At default presolve ($n=\ConeN$ solves per arm) the default-scaling arm's incumbents violate their cones within tolerance, with an objective effect of median \ConeDefMed\ and max \ConeDefMax\ of $|V|$; for the rescaled arm it is at most \ConeRescMax.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Objective scaling and weight scaling.} N2(a) repeats the base instances with $N=\NOneMidN$ at $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ and \SObj\ (\NTwoSolves\ solves; Table~\ref{tab:n2}). Objective scaling governs the absolute tolerances of branch and bound. At $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ big-M stops at the WorkLimit in \NTwoBigMWLOne\ instances, with median certified gap \NTwoBigMGapOne\ and median Work \NTwoBigMWorkOne; at \SObj\ the gap is \NTwoBigMGapScaled\ and the Work \NTwoBigMWorkScaled. Weight scaling governs the cones and does not replace objective scaling. At $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$, at \DIb\ with $K=\FalseCertK$, the rescaled perspective reported a closed gap while its $B_{\mathrm{eff}}$ lay \FalseCertGap$|V|$ below big-M's polished value: a false certificate. At \SObj\ no incumbent exceeds another arm's bound (\NTwoBeatsScaled, against \NTwoBeatsOne\ at $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$), and at either scale no disagreement exceeds the larger claimed gap (\NTwoBeyond\ of \NTwoPairs\ pairs over both scales). N2(b) solves \prb\ through CVXPY \cite{diamond2016cvxpy} at the dates \NTwoConvexDates\ against Clarabel at tolerance \NTwoRefTol. Gurobi's barrier on the unscaled QCQP errs by up to \BarrierRawA\ in $A^*$ and \BarrierRawDual\ in the binding duals, and objective scaling reduces these to \BarrierScaledA\ and \BarrierScaledDual. Normalizing the risk row to right-hand side one changes nothing for the barrier. The written models differ in exactly \ProbeLines\ row on all \ProbeN\ date and scaling pairs, and $A^*$ is identical with and without it at default settings (\ProbeSameDefault\ of \ProbeN) and with Gurobi's scaling off (\ProbeSameScale), but not with presolve off, where it differs by up to \ProbePresolveMax. Finally, in \HedgedRelax\ of \HedgedRelaxN\ perspective relaxations, \HedgedNames\ names hold both legs (largest smaller leg \HedgedMaxLeg), each with net weight below $\ell$ and $z^++z^-$ above $|w^+-w^-|/\ell$ (\HedgedHolds\ of \HedgedNames, as predicted): the relaxation hedges to cheapen its cone.

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}
\begin{outline}{V, 1.0 page; DESIGN §11.4 and the S4 addendum item 6}
\item Modeling choice, fixed risk budget against fixed $\lambda$: costs at equal risk; mean-variance recovered at $\lambda^*$ (A1) $\rightarrow$ \KFourLam.
\item Modeling choice, $\lambda^*$ fixed within (date, $N$) for \pmi: a Lagrangian relaxation of the risk row, exact only without integers; the MIQP's volatility can fall below the budget $\rightarrow$ not yet reported (open item: DESIGN §3.4 asks for it).
\item Modeling choices: single period with $w_0=0$; the six-factor, \RiskWindow-day risk model with the residual floor; the momentum construction and winsorization; the base mandate values; the \MiqpPositionPct\% cap and $\ell$ in \pmi; costs as assumptions $\rightarrow$ Table~\ref{tab:mandate}.
\item Limitations: the disclosures below.
\item Trade-off, alpha against exposure: the cost curves $\rightarrow$ Fig.~\ref{fig:costcurves}, \CTwoLiqTight, \CTwoSectorTight.
\item Trade-off, formulation strength against per-node cost: tighter at the root, but cone nodes $\rightarrow$ \KTwentyFourMed; median nodes at base \NodesBigMBase\ (big-M), \NodesRescBase\ (rescaled), \NodesDefBase\ (default).
\item Trade-off, tightness against effort $\rightarrow$ Fig.~\ref{fig:formulations}.
\item Trade-off, tolerance against runtime: MIPGap \IOneMipGap\ (I1) against \NOneMipGap\ (N1); Work at $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ $\rightarrow$ \NTwoBigMWorkOne\ against \NTwoBigMWorkScaled.
\item What each estimator measures (A8), and why the errors depend on $\delta$ $\rightarrow$ \RobustPerspFive\ against \RobustPerspTen\ at \IOneRobustDate.
\item Two failure modes: a support change within the step for the fixed-integer dual (P3 \PredThreeMed; P1 \PredOneMax), and relaxation looseness for the relaxation slopes (Spearman \SpearmanPersp, \SpearmanBigM; perspective per class \ClassPerspPOne, \ClassPerspPThree) $\rightarrow$ results/s3b\_analysis/ item 3.
\item The I2 near-tie (Decision 44): median secant \NearTieSector\ (sector) against \NearTieMom\ (momentum); under the perspective slope the order flips, \NearTiePerspSector\ against \NearTiePerspMom.
\item Unexpected: presolve does big-M's root work $\rightarrow$ \PreBigMRootOn\ against \PreBigMRootOff; Work \PreBigMWorkOn\ against \PreBigMWorkOff.
\item Unexpected: the false certificate at $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ $\rightarrow$ \FalseCertGap.
\item Unexpected: the risk-row normalization is absorbed by presolve (supported, not proven) $\rightarrow$ \ProbeSameDefault\ of \ProbeN, \ProbePresolveMax.
\item Unexpected: the hedged legs; per-leg cones as an extension $\rightarrow$ \HedgedNames, \HedgedHolds.
\item K29b-ext: slope accuracy holds on every I1 case, not only the gated ones $\rightarrow$ \ExtWithin\ of \ExtN.
\item The earlier iteration's lessons in one or two sentences, without numbers: the fixed-risk formulation and the scaling policy.
\item Extensions: platform coordination by exposure prices (decomposition); multi-period rebalancing (MPC); robust alpha (SOCP); a Lagrangian bound for the cardinality row.
\end{outline}

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}
\begin{outline}{VI, 0.25 page}
\item Q1: neutrality is cheap for a weakly aligned alpha; caps and sector bounds carry the cost $\rightarrow$ \ELiqMed, \IdealRetMomMin.
\item Q2: duals stop being prices once integers enter; the fixed-integer dual is exact only on a stable support $\rightarrow$ \PredOneMax, \PredThreeMed, Table~\ref{tab:i1}.
\item Q3: the perspective formulation helps only with its weights rescaled, and objective scaling is still needed $\rightarrow$ \RootRescBase, \RootDefBase, \FalseCertGap.
\item Extensions $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:discussion}.
\end{outline}
